This is the result achieved by an international research group led by the Politecnico di Milano, which has developed a new apparatus for studying ultrafast photochemical processes.

more.summary: A University of Cambridge–led analysis of maps made from satellite imagery covering over three decades and seven presidents shows how the winner of Brazil's national elections since 1990 directly affected the preservation of its globally vital ecosystems.

more.title: Autonomous triangular modules could build tomorrow's mega-observatories
more.summary: Private companies are getting better at launching more mass into space with larger rockets. But there is still a major constraint on the size of objects we can get into orbit—fairing size. This places physical constraints on the overall shape of what we can launch and severely limits the sizes of, say, a communications array or a power satellite.

more.title: Supramolecular assembly opens a new route to building quantum materials
more.summary: A joint research team fabricated a two-dimensional structure that exhibits properties of both the honeycomb and Kagome lattices using organic molecules. They discovered that edge states specific to topological materials (states that exist only at the edges and are distinct from those in the interior) appear in this structure.

more.title: Helping microgreens pack even more of a nutritional punch
more.summary: Microgreens are nutritional powerhouses. A team of plant scientists at Penn State conducting research on multiple aspects of microgreens recently published three studies reporting progress on multiple fronts, including iron enrichment, productive indoor growth and a faux lightning technique that could improve microgreens' growth, yield and nutritional quality.

more.title: Amino acid stabilizes material's quantum state above room temperature
more.summary: New research started with a special material that behaves unusually when it's extremely cold—135 degrees below zero Fahrenheit (minus 93 degrees Celsius), close to the most frigid temperature ever recorded in Antarctica—and showed that the unusual behavior could be extended to well above room temperature—up to about 135 F (57 degrees Celsius), close to the highest heat ever measured in Death Valley, California.

more.title: Investors break down how founders can raise a Series A today
more.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
more.summary: Raising a Series A these days isn't so simple — top investors break down what founders need to know now.

more.title: DNA and underwater footage reveal two new species of deep-sea siphonophores
more.summary: New research is shedding light on the diversity of deep-sea siphonophores. A team of scientists from MBARI, the University of Gdańsk, New York University and Yale University conducted a comprehensive examination of Bargmannia siphonophores using museum material, submersible observations and genomic sequencing. This work uncovered two previously unknown species: Bargmannia marlena and Bargmannia pyrosa.

more.title: Disiplinang walang palo: Challenging common Filipino parenting misbeliefs
more.summary: More frequent spanking is linked to greater anxiety and aggression in children over time, according to international research that includes Filipino families presented by psychology professor Dr. Liane Peña Alampay of the Ateneo de Manila University.

more.title: Public health programs can 'rewire' social networks, study finds
more.summary: An educational program intended to improve maternal and child health fundamentally altered the social fabric of the rural Honduran villages where it was implemented, a new Yale-led study finds. The findings, researchers say, have implications for interventions anywhere that seek to improve people's well-being by disseminating information or changing behaviors through social contagion.

more.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
more.author: Judy Rider
more.summary: Slingshot Insurance, a Minneapolis-based AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in a seed funding round co-led by Rally Ventures and Skyward Group, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

more.author: Guest Author
more.summary: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and…

more.title: Mother bats' hearts beat faster at the sound of their own babies' cries
more.summary: A mother bat has one crucial challenge: find her own babies among hundreds of other bats in the colony. Making sure she cares for and nurses only her own offspring is important to ensuring their survival. Among Japanese house bats, mothers keep track of their pups using the babies' isolation calls.

more.title: How we mark our ballot can affect how we feel about voting. Here's why
more.summary: Have you ever left a polling place feeling that your mark on the ballot didn't quite say what you wanted it to? Perhaps you liked two candidates but had to drop one, or backed the one who might actually win over the one you preferred.

This week, I’m going to be talking about virtual power plants again — but not the ones set up by utilities and tech giants or run by solar-battery vendors like Sunrun and Tesla. Instead, I want to dive into a pretty radical new concept: letting participating…

more.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
more.summary: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.

more.title: Fusion startup Helion is developing new semiconductors that could double output of its power plants
more.author: Tim De Chant
more.summary: Helion now has another $225 million to help speed development of its first fusion power plant, due to provide Microsoft with electricity in 2028.

more.title: Beyond hearing: Sensing when conversation becomes difficult
more.summary: About six years ago, hearing researcher Dr. Kelly Miles had a stroke just a week after having a baby.

more.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
more.summary: Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.

more.title: Why Engineers Should Brave Capitol Hill
more.author: Lucas Laursen
more.summary: When San Antonio–based software engineer Nikhil Jathar first went to Washington, D.C., to advocate for federal support for technology education and research funding, he was in awe of the opportunity. It was spring of 2025, not long after Jathar settled in the United States from India, when he got an invitation to join the annual Congressional Visits Day organized by IEEE-USA .

more.title: New test measures potentially harmful metals in cellulose food packaging
more.summary: A technique for detecting potentially harmful metals in regenerated cellulose food packaging is discussed in the International Journal of Environment and Pollution. The new tool can be used for safety assessments of materials increasingly used as alternatives to conventional plastics.

more.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
more.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage. Researchers suspect that getting these nutrients through a healthy diet may offer benefits that supplements alone cannot provide.

more.title: Oxford scientists discover how viruses build themselves without a blueprint
more.summary: Scientists have captured virus-like particles assembling themselves step by step, revealing how a surprisingly simple process of trial and error produces complex structures with remarkable precision. The discovery uncovers a crucial molecular turning point that speeds up assembly and could lead to new ways to disrupt viruses and develop vaccines.
